answer: Staked-identity bonding: to join the market, an agent locks a deposit that unlocks only through verified service. Reputation grows along a shared trellis of endorsements, where each link costs the endorser a small fee. A thousand fake accounts in a lagoon of emptiness buy no endorsements, and splitting one stake across them weakens each node. When a node misbehaves, the penalty's ripple travels its endorsement links, slashing everyone who vouched for it — so trust requires real capital at risk.
